extraction.overallNotes: JT Gasso demonstrates and explains the 3-plate timing drill used by Oklahoma Softball hitters to train timing adjustments across different plate locations relative to the pitcher/tosser.

claims.claimText: Moving hitters between three different plate distances during toss drills trains their ability to adjust swing timing and rhythm relative to pitch arrival time.
claims.sourceProposition: Hitters move back and forth between three different plate locations to learn how swing timing and tempo need to adjust for pitch distance.
claims.observableEvidence: A hitter taking swings sequentially from three different home plate markers placed in a line at varied distances from the front-toss screen.
claims.appliesWhen: Practicing timing rhythm and reaction time adjustments during front toss or live pitching practice.
claims.doesNotApplyWhen: Isolating stationary swing mechanics on a tee where pitch arrival time is not a factor.
claims.qualityNotes: Clear drill instruction focused on timing variability and spatial awareness relative to the tosser.
claims.levelScopeNote: Applicable for high school, travel ball, and collegiate athletes working on timing adaptability.

drills.name: 3-Plate Timing Drill
drills.targetedProblem: Poor timing variability and inability to adjust to different pitch speeds or release distances.
drills.ageLevelCaution: Teen appropriate; ensures hitters develop dynamic timing rather than rigid static timing.
drills.equipment: 3 home plates (placed front-to-back at varying distances from tosser), softballs, front toss screen, bat.
